doc.title: Buddy Tate interviewed by Michael Woods, Scottsdale, Arizona, March 3, 1995

chapter: Georgette's memories of the Basie band
title: Running onstage at the Roxy; Lena, Dinah, Sarah and Billie Holiday
summary: Georgette and Pepper wandered onstage at the Roxy; she recalls meeting Lena Horne, Sarah Vaughan and Billie Holiday, and Tate praises Billie's song choices.

story.theme_name: Singers and the musicians who accompanied them
story.community_name: Billie Holiday as the musicians knew her

blocks.x: I was so embarrassed because I had my slip on, and I said, “why is everybody asking me these questions and they see I have on my slip.” That’s all I could think about. And my mother said, “are you all right?” “I’m fine.” And you know they were worried. But I was concerned that everybody saw me in my slip. I mean these are the kind of stories that Judy and I would, we would, it was always an experience. Always, always. I remember Basie would play and they had a show and there was chorus girls and they had great big satin balls. And the girls would be on top of the ball and they would come across. And I remember Pepper and I, we saw our parents playing on stage, and we didn’t know the show had started, and we ran out on stage, and then we look out and there was all these people —
In the big Roxy Theater. © Hamilton College Jazz Archive -13-
And they were looking at us. And everybody start to laugh and then we’d laugh. And then they’d clap and then we’d clap. And Basie said, “would you please” —

I can remember all the lights and all the beautiful people. I remember so many, I remember Lena, watching her make up her face, and saying when I get big I want to be like her. I remember, oh, I can’t think of her name you just said it — Carmen?
No, as a child I think, Dinah Washington —
Sarah Vaughan, I met them all, and I loved Billie Holiday. I loved Billie. She was, I just loved Billie she was special, very special.

Yes she had ... her choice of songs were different. She would sing like “Good Morning Heartache,” and she’d pick the right songs, and just for her. I guess it was because she’d lived a, you know, a sad life. And “Good Morning Heartache,” “Fine and Mellow,” and what was the next one she sang she used to do, I can’t even remember, but I dug her choice. Nat King Cole was another one, picked the right songs to sing.
